# General Remarks

You will

:::incremental
- read scientific papers to build a theoretical foundation,
- apply findings in exercises and case analyses,
- build a personal latticework of leadership mental models,
- research an assigned (digital) leader and one specific leadership situation, and
- analyze that situation using the theories discussed in the course.
:::

This is an **examination-only term.** There are no lectures in the winter term 2026/2027, so you study the lecture notes of the summer term 2026 on your own and build a personal **latticework of mental models for leadership** from them.

As a graded exam assignment, you present your assigned leader and a leadership situation you select yourself, and then analyze that situation in a Q&A with the examiner.

# Contents

In this semester no lecture will be offered. Thus, you need to study the lecture notes on your own. These notes cover topics from self-awareness through interpersonal influence to organizational and ecosystem-level leadership, helping you understand leadership at multiple levels:

- [**Foundations & mental models**](../../26ST/foundations/index.html) (latticework thinking, decision-making under complexity, the digital leadership context)
- [**The leader**](../../26ST/leader/index.html) (traits, emotional intelligence, self-awareness, evolution of leadership thought)
- [**Adaptive leadership**](../../26ST/adaptive-behavior/index.html) (paradoxes, competing values, behavioral complexity, situational approaches)
- [**Motivating & engaging followers**](../../26ST/motivation/index.html) (path-goal theory, self-determination theory, engaging leadership)
- [**Building high-performing teams**](../../26ST/team/index.html) (team development, psychological safety, diversity & inclusion, virtual teams)
- [**Conflict, power & politics**](../../26ST/conflict-power/index.html) (conflict dynamics, sources of power, lateral leadership, organizational politics)
- [**Stakeholder management & coalitions**](../../26ST/stakeholder/index.html) (social capital theory, stakeholder mapping, engagement strategies, coalition building)
- [**Leadership in context**](../../26ST/context/index.html) (cross-cultural leadership, ethical and sustainable leadership, adaptive leadership for digital transformation)
- [**Storytelling**](../../26ST/communication/index.html) (narrative as a leadership tool, persuasion, stakeholder communication)

# Learning Objectives

You should improve your ability to consciously use, reflect on and further develop your leadership skills, in particular with regard to

::: incremental
- *leadership requirements* in the context of digital transformation and VUCA environments,
- identification of and reflection on your own leadership traits, strengths, and development areas,
- understanding and navigating leadership paradoxes and competing demands using adaptive approaches,
- creating conditions for follower motivation and work engagement,
- building and leading high-performing, psychologically safe, and diverse teams,
- analyzing and managing power dynamics, conflict, and organizational politics,
- systematic stakeholder identification, analysis, and engagement across multi-stakeholder environments, and
- communicating with impact using storytelling and narrative techniques.
:::

# Effort

You will gain 5 ECTS for this course. This equals approx. __150 hours workload__, of which you need most to pass the course.

# Examination

The examination has two parts:

:::incremental
- a **presentation** of approximately 8 minutes, in which you portray your assigned leader and one specific leadership situation, and
- a **Q&A** of approximately 8 minutes, in which the examiner asks you to analyze that situation using the theories discussed in the course.
:::

The Q&A carries the larger share of the grade (30 % presentation, 70 % Q&A). Details see [here](../assignment/index.qmd).
